mbm-0826.clue: I only use the quiet side at night.
mbm-0826.quote: Mum’s patchwork picnics are all bright checks and stripes. On the back of her quilt I stitched a dark window with one little yellow square of light. She turns that side up at bedtime.

mbm-0827.clue: I always make space for a tiny shoe.
mbm-0827.quote: I stitched a leather key case shaped like my baby brother’s first boot. Dad keeps patting his pocket and grinning. That boot finally takes him somewhere.

mbm-0828.clue: I have a villain who pays in buttons.
mbm-0828.quote: I write stories on the bus. A lost red button rolled beneath my seat just as my burglar reached the toll bridge. Now every copy of that chapter has a red button drawn in the margin.

mbm-0829.clue: I keep a leaf with my scorecards.
mbm-0829.quote: I chipped my ball over an old maple and watched it land beside a red leaf on the green. My playing partner pressed the leaf into my scorebook. Only one of us remembers the score.

mbm-0830.clue: I made a throne for the lost checker.
mbm-0830.quote: Our game box had a checker from a completely different set. I glued a tiny paper crown to it. Now whoever clears the table first gets to move the king.

mbm-0831.clue: I measured the stool before the cat.
mbm-0831.quote: I crocheted a square cushion for the footstool. Our cat claimed it before I finished weaving in the last end. I had to tie the knot under one sleeping paw.

mbm-0832.clue: I know the weather by the pajama pile.
mbm-0832.quote: Our family watches monster movies in flannel. Every time the creature appears, another pillow goes over somebody’s eyes. I can tell how good the movie was by how tall the pile gets.

mbm-0833.clue: I got the station clock in my sketch.
mbm-0833.quote: I drew the same train three Sundays running. The last time the driver leaned out and pointed at my drawing. I’d drawn every wheel but forgotten the station clock behind him.

mbm-0834.clue: I’ve danced with an empty sleeve.
mbm-0834.quote: Our folk-dance circle kept a space for a friend whose bus ran late. I waved her scarf through every turn. When she slipped into the gap the scarf landed right around her shoulders.

mbm-0835.clue: I own half a blue ribbon.
mbm-0835.quote: My partner and I tied for last at our first ballroom social. The hostess cut a blue ribbon in half for us anyway. We bow to each other with our scraps pinned inside our cuffs.

mbm-0836.clue: I take my sketchbook to the baggage fence.
mbm-0836.quote: A biplane landed with one red wheel and one yellow one. I drew them both before the mechanic tucked it away. My nephew insists it’s a plane in mismatched socks.

mbm-0837.clue: My towel has a white stripe down the middle.
mbm-0837.quote: I learned to slalom by lining up the red roof on shore with the boat’s wake. My sister held up a striped towel like a finish flag each time I made it back upright.

mbm-0838.clue: I look for the second-best view.
mbm-0838.quote: The sightseeing line to the famous tower went around the block. I climbed the bakery steps across the street and found the whole tower reflected in a puddle beside my shoes.

mbm-0839.clue: My clay owl has a practical profession.
mbm-0839.quote: I made an owl whose eyes came out too large. The hollow eyes hold my pencils, and the crooked beak holds my eraser. He looks overworked whenever I’m drawing.

mbm-0840.clue: I know the song that fixes my shoes.
mbm-0840.quote: At the club I snapped a silver shoelace just before our favorite record. My friend pulled a ribbon off her wrist and laced me back in on the beat. We made the chorus.

mbm-0841.clue: I keep a green marble for emergencies.
mbm-0841.quote: Our mini-golf windmill needed a counterweight. The owner tried my lucky marble in the little bucket. The sails finally turned, and my next putt went between them.

mbm-0842.clue: I can waltz with a grocery bag.
mbm-0842.quote: My ballroom partner was traveling, so I practiced turns in Mum’s kitchen with a bag of oranges. When one rolled out, Mum caught it on the third beat and joined me for the next turn.

mbm-0843.clue: I once mailed a steam engine to my sister.
mbm-0843.quote: I drew the old train passing the bridge on the back of a postcard. When she held it beside her window, the little painted engine looked ready to cross her garden fence.

mbm-0844.clue: I have a hat that crossed the pond alone.
mbm-0844.quote: My straw hat blew off the canoe and landed brim up. We paddled beside it until a ripple carried it to the boat ramp. It won the race by two lengths.

mbm-0845.clue: I listen to my climbing partner’s shoes.
mbm-0845.quote: On the last move I couldn’t see a foothold. My friend tapped it twice with her shoe from the ledge beside me. I followed the sound and we stood on the ledge together.

mbm-0846.clue: I’ve learned to dodge the blue sock.
mbm-0846.quote: I taught my cousins to juggle rolled socks over the couch. One blue bundle keeps opening in midair like a parachute. Whoever catches it gets to pick the next song.

mbm-0847.clue: I’ve collected red squares since I was twelve.
mbm-0847.quote: I sewed them into a quilt shaped like a theater curtain. Two pieces pull apart in the middle to show a tiny stitched stage. My niece put her first finger puppet right there.

mbm-0848.clue: I wrapped a whole summer in a biscuit tin.
mbm-0848.quote: I kept fabric scraps from every summer picnic, then stitched one tiny pennant from each. The quilt lays them out like flags above a long green table, right down to the jam stains.

mbm-0849.clue: I always save the end of the reel.
mbm-0849.quote: Our neighborhood theater lets me help coil the leader after the last showing. One frame held a hand-drawn star from an old projectionist. I took a picture of it under the little desk lamp.

mbm-0850.clue: I measure bedtime in little blue boats.
mbm-0850.quote: I stitched a row of boats from different blues in our scrap bag. My nephew sails his finger along them at bedtime, and he almost never reaches the boat with the gingham sail.
